chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Ali ibn al-Samit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

We were with him at a funeral, and some of the people said: 'May Allah bless me in death and in what comes after death.' He (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What comes after death is a favor/excellence; if you are blessed in death, you are indeed blessed in what comes after it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct understanding of blessing in death versus blessing in the afterlife according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refines the theological understanding of posthumous blessings by distinguishing between the moment of death and the enduring state of the soul in Barzakh. He establishes a logical hierarchy where blessing in death is the prerequisite and encompassing cause for blessing in the afterlife, thereby elevating the supplicant's hope for eternal felicity. This insight reflects the Shia emphasis on the continuity of divine mercy beyond the grave, linking the physical transition with spiritual permanence.

en.basel-kadem: 12.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said:

We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from Yahya bin Ibrahim, from Abu’l-Bilad, from his father, from Abdullah bin ‘Ataa’, that he said: I said to Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him: Indeed, people are saying: Indeed, Ali bin Abi Talib, Allah’s blessings be upon him, said: «Indeed, the best ihram is that you perform ihram from the circle of your people.» He said: Abu Ja’far, peace be upon him, then died that and said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, was among the people of Medina, yet his time was fixed at Dhu’l-Halifa, and it was six miles [1] between them. If it was an act of virtue, the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, had surely performed ihram from Medina. Rather, Ali, Allah’s blessings be upon him, used to say: Perform tamattu’ [2] with your clothes until your fixed time.
